chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Zarih al-Muharbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The best of aids toward the Hereafter is the world.

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: The world, worldly life, the present temporal existence
key_terms.الْآخِرَةِ: The Hereafter, the next world, the eternal life
key_terms.نِعْمَ: How excellent / the best of (a formula of high praise in Arabic, often used for superlatives)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the relationship between the world and the Hereafter?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that worldly life, far from being an obstacle to spiritual attainment, is the finest means of preparing for the Hereafter. This concise aphorism reflects the Shia Islamic understanding that the world is a farm (mazra'ah) for the afterlife — that proper, purposeful use of worldly means, such as earning, charity, and righteous deeds performed within this life, is the very vehicle for earning one's place in the eternal realm. The original audience of Imam al-Sadiq's followers would have understood 'the world' (al-dunya) not as material pleasure for its own sake, but as the arena of action and opportunity that, when used wisely, becomes the greatest helper in achieving salvation.
